To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified 10 putative chitin biosynthesis genes in the cephalocordate Branchiastoma floridae and nine of these genes show novel domain architectures that might be important for the interaction with the extracellular environment.

we have identified a large number of chitin synthase genes in the cephalichordate Branchiosta floridae and that they show a mosaic structure with novel domains never described in other chitin synthases, suggesting a role in the extracellular matrix.
we identified 12 genes coding for proteins with conserved amino acid motifs of processive glycostransferases from GT2 fungal family in the cephalocordate Branchiastoma floridae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel chitin synthases with mosaic structures in B. floridae, which might be involved in the formation of the extracellular matrix in early chordates.
the evolution of the ECM in the early evolution of Metazoans, with a focus on the origin and evolution of chitin synthase genes.
the origin of chitin synthase genes in Metazoa and the possible role of these proteins in the ECM of B. floridae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chitin is present in B. floridae and that the chitin synthases involved in this process are characterized by a mosaic structure.
chitin synthases have a more general role in metazoan development and that the presence of chitinous ECMs is more widespread than previously thought.

the presence of chitinous ECM in B. floridae and other chordate species is not due to the presence of CHSs, but rather to other enzymes, which have not been characterized yet, and that the CHSs identified in the present study are not related to chitinous ECM, but to other functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of chitosaccharides and the related enzymes in B. floridae is not an evolutionary novelty, rather a remnant of a primordial state, which is still present in this species.

the presence of chitinous structures in the pharyngea of cephalochordates is likely to be due to the expression of chitin synthase genes with mosaic structure and novel domains, which might be involved in the interaction with the extracellular environment.
the presence of chitooligosacchrides and chitin synthases with novel domains in the cephalichordate B. floridae might suggest a more general role of these molecules in the development of Metazoans.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of chitinous structures and the occurrence of chitinous genes in lower chordates might be more widespread than previously thought, and that the presence of a chitin-based ECM might have played a crucial role in the evolution of Metazoans.
the evolution of the ECM in Metazoans is more complex than previously thought, as chitin synthases are present in a wider range of organisms and display a mosaic architecture.
, in the context of the evolution of the extracellular matrix, the acquisition and/or diversification of novel domains might be a key event for the establishment of a new extracellular matrix.
